import { Callout } from 'nextra/components'

# Migrate from XRootD Cache (v1) to v2 Cache

We use the term v1 cache to refer to XRootD cache, and v2 cache to refer to the Go-native cache implemented by Pelican itself.

<Callout type="warning">
  V2 cache is an experimental feature.
  `Cache.EnableV2` is still a hidden configuration parameter as of this writing.
</Callout>

## Migration steps

We assume the `pelican-server` process is running as root user and the configuration file is at `/etc/pelican/pelican.yaml`, the default location.

1. Make sure that you are running a v1 cache.
   Run `pelican-server config dump | grep -in 'EnableV2'`
   The output should be `EnableV2: false`.
   If you are already running a v2 cache, there is no need for migration.
2. Gracefully terminate the cache.
   Please refrain from using `kill -9 <cache_pid>` to terminate the cache forcefully.
3. Set `Cache.EnableV2: true` in the configuration file of the cache.
4. Since v2 cache serves objects from [`Server.WebPort`](/parameters#Server-WebPort), not [`Cache.Port`](/parameters#Cache-Port), adjust your firewall rules accordingly.
   Close `Cache.Port`, and make sure your firewall rules allow clients to reach `Server.WebPort`.
5. Restart the cache.
   The cache should be launched successfully.
   There is no need to register the cache again.
6. Optionally delete the data and metadata of cached objects left by v1 cache.
   See note 4 below for details.

## Notes

1. After switching to v2 cache, the file system path where v2 cache stores the data and metadata of cached objects will be `${Cache.StorageLocation}/persistent-cache`.
2. V2 cache uses a different storage layout from v1 cache.
   On v2 cache, the data of each object is stored as a series of chunks on the underlying file system, and its metadata is stored in [BadgerDB](https://github.com/dgraph-io/badger).
   Given this change, the data formats used by v1 and v2 cache are not compatible with each other.
3. Since v2 cache cannot inherit cached objects from v1, it will start cold.
4. The cache will not delete the data and metadata left by v1 cache.
   If you wish to save the disk space, you will need to delete them manually by yourself.
   The data and metadata used by v1 cache is under `${Cache.StorageLocation}/{data,meta,namespace}` by default.
   If you ever changed [`Cache.StorageLocation`](/parameters#Cache-StorageLocation), [`Cache.NamespaceLocation`](/parameters#Cache-NamespaceLocation), [`Cache.MetaLocations`](/parameters#Cache-MetaLocations), or [`Cache.DataLocations`](/parameters#Cache-DataLocations), find and delete the corresponding directories by following them.
   However, doing so will make the cache become cold if you want to rollback to v1 cache later.

## Rollback

It is possible to rollback to v1 cache from v2:

1. Make sure you are running a v2 cache.
2. Terminate the cache gracefully.
3. Set `Cache.EnableV2: false`.
4. Since v1 cache serves objects from `Cache.Port`, not `Server.WebPort`, adjust your firewall rules accordingly.
   Make sure `Cache.Port` is reachable from clients, and consider restricting `Server.WebPort`, because clients don't need to reach it now.
5. Restart the cache.
   The cache should be able to start successfully.
   There is no need to register the cache again.
6. Optionally, delete the data and metadata of the cached objects left by v2 cache.
   However, by doing so, your v2 cache will start cold if you wish to migrate to v2 again.
